text:
anya: quick sync — proposing a 'slimline affinity' export from the policy engine: instead of emitting a full ranked route list, policy returns per-tenant affinity buckets + lightweight constraints (hot/warm/cold, region_hints, hard_excludes) and a small penalty vector. goal: reduce policy eval churn and make hot-reloads cheaper. thoughts?

jon: +1 to reducing surface area. main concern — how do we represent *hard* requirements (e.g., compliance region-only) vs soft preferences? need explicit fields, otherwise runtime might pick incompatible routes.

rachel: agree. my rough shape: policy -> { bucket: "hot|warm|cold", region_hints: ["us-west-2"], hard_exclude: ["eu-central-1"], affinity_version: "vN", reasoning_id: "policy-123" } and runtime still does route scoring and final assignment. keeps policy small but expressive.

liam: capacity signal is a runtime-only input though. since scoring is moved to runtime, do we hardcode scoring formula or expose scoring weights as part of the policy output?

anya: prefer keeping weights runtime-configured (pluggable weight vector). policy shouldn't tune for instantaneous capacity. policy provides constraints + penalties; runtime composes capacity, local load, and those penalties to score. benefit: policy reloads don't force large rebalances.

jon: downside: less deterministic outcomes — two runtimes with different weight defaults could diverge. mitigation: policy should include `recommended_weight_vector` and `explainability` metadata: policy_id, bucket_reason, sample_keys to allow replay and debugging.

rachel: also need cache key semantics. when affinity changes we must invalidate prefix caches. propose policy emits `affinity_version` and `affected_prefixes` so runtime can evict relevant prefix/KV caches.

anya: rollout proposal: 1) shadow mode where policy emits both old ranked list + new buckets (no-op for runtime). 2) canary runtime that honors buckets for a single tenant or region. 3) ramp with telemetry gates.

infra-bot: @channel deploy-bot: canary deployment started on infra-canary-7, image=redwood/runtime:canary-2026-03-20 (logs at https://ci.internal/canaries/infra-canary-7)

liam: telemetry gates we should track: route divergence rate (ranked-list vs runtime-resolved), success_rate per bucket, p50/p95 latencies per bucket, and eviction churn. suggest gate: if divergence > 5% for 10m or p95 increases > 20% for a bucket, rollback.

jon: implementation note re: matchers — we could keep current matcher DSL and compile into a sidecar-runner, or compile to WASM for sandboxing + language-agnostic plugins. WASM pros: isolation and reuse; cons: binary size, cold-start perf. maybe start DSL->sidecar runner and iterate to WASM for heavy tenants.

rachel: testing matrix: unit tests for policy->bucket mapping, deterministic simulation (policy+buckets + runtime weight vector -> expected route distribution), integration with capacity shim, and chaos test for region outage to validate hard_exclude semantics.

anya: open action items I will take: 1) draft a follow-up RFC with proto fields (bucket enum, region_hints, hard_exclude, affinity_version, recommended_weight_vector, explainability payload shape), 2) add rollout checklist and telemetry SLO gates, 3) docs/SDK change note for customers.

liam: I can help wire telemetry and the divergence calc tomorrow.

rachel: adding one UX ask — operator view in Console to show policy_id + last_affinity_version + a diff view vs previous version (helps on-call).

jon: also record migration hedges: keep ranked list fallback in runtime for N weeks and a per-tenant opt-out flag.

anya: thanks all. I'll file the RFC follow-up and link PR here when ready. :thumbsup: :shipit:

liam: ack.

rachel: thanks — looking forward to the RFC.

anya: closing this thread, moving checklist to the RFC PR.
